When SFINAE Is Still Relevant in C++23

Even with concepts and if constexpr in C++23, SFINAE (via std::enable_if and similar techniques) still has its place in very specific cases, especially where:
Partial Specialization of Templates: Concepts cannot be used to partially specialize a template for certain types,
so SFINAE is useful when you need to define different behavior forspecialized template types.

Fallback Logic in Overloaded Functions: For cases where function overloads need to differentiate based on type traits
that can’t easily be captured by concepts alone (like when you needmultiple overloads for different combinations of traits).
Advanced Type Manipulation: For complex template metaprogramming tasks where you need to manipulate or transform types in ways
that go beyond what concepts currently offer. This includesusing SFINAE to select types based on more nuanced conditions.
